U3: Setup UI infrastructure to integrate admin_ui and Flo.

- Use Spring XD's module extension points to implement custom Kafka encoders/decoders.
- Implement gpfdist and gpload as standard Spring XD modules/tasklets.
- Decouple Hadoop dependencies by moving them to optional module-specific classloaders rather than the root classloader.

technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring XD's module extension points to implement and inject custom Kafka encoders and decoders.
Implement gpfdist and gpload as standard Spring XD sink modules and tasklets respectively.
Decouple Hadoop dependencies by moving them to optional, module-specific classloaders rather than the root classloader.
Implement dynamic classpath resolution using Spring's ResourcePatternResolver and custom module classloaders.
Adopt a tasklet-based approach for file reading to avoid memory overhead associated with message bus streams.
assumptions: The developer is familiar with Spring XD, Kafka, GPDB/HAWQ, and Spring Framework internals.
Necessary development and testing environments (including GPDB, HAWQ, and Kafka instances) are already set up and accessible.
UI infrastructure tools (admin_ui and Flo) are already developed and only require integration into the Spring XD environment.
The effort estimate covers design, development, unit testing, and integration testing, but excludes project management and production deployment.
Java 17+ and Spring Framework 6.0+ are used as the baseline environment.

activities.activity_description: Design and implement the ability to customize encoders and decoders used by the Kafka source, sink, and bus in Spring XD (U1).
Develop an out-of-the-box gpfdist sink module to enable ultra-fast data movement from various sources into GPDB/HAWQ (U2).
Set up the UI infrastructure required to integrate admin_ui and Flo into the Spring XD environment (U3).
Create an end-to-end Kafka use-case to study, demonstrate, and verify a Kafka + XD play built for scale and performance (U4).
Implement an efficient tasklet-based approach to read files without reading line-by-line or keeping content in-memory (U5).
Create a gpload tasklet to ingest data from various sources into GPDB in an efficient manner (U6).
Remove Hadoop dependencies from the root classpath to avoid classloading penalties at startup and decouple for non-HDFS module registry situations (U7).
Add support for dynamic classpath for modules, allowing flexibility to load dependencies based on module options or specific locations (U8).
Perform end-to-end integration testing of all new modules and features, and update relevant documentation.
